teams.heading: Andrew Durutalo appointed Fiji Rugby Union's new Head of Men's High Performance
teams.body: Former United States international Andrew Durutalo has returned to Suva after being named to lead the national pathways. The former academy pioneer is tasked with aligning development structures from under-18 level through to the Flying Fijians, whilst focusing on retaining domestic talent. High Performance General Manager Nacani Cawanibuka emphasised the strategic appointment, stating: "Our focus is not only on preparing national teams for the next competition."

lead.why: The appointment of Andrew Durutalo as Head of Men's High Performance marks a major structural step for Fiji's pathways and talent retention.

teams.heading: Stuart Barnes has condemned the RFU for extending Steve Borthwick's England contract
teams.body: Former England fly-half Stuart Barnes has heavily criticised the RFU for handing Steve Borthwick a contract extension until 2028, accusing the governing body of an 'ostrich policy'. Writing in The Times, Barnes labelled Borthwick's tenure a 'failure' after a disastrous Six Nations campaign that included an embarrassing defeat to Italy. Despite subsequent victories over Fiji and Argentina, Barnes argued that the team's poor performances have reduced England to a 'second-tier Six Nations side'.

teams.heading: The IRFU rejects World Rugby proposals to host games in America
teams.body: The IRFU has confirmed there are currently no plans or discussions to stage a Six Nations match in the United States. While World Rugby chief executive Alan Gilpin had floated the prospect of moving fixtures—specifically citing a potential Ireland versus Italy encounter to leverage expatriate fanbases—the Irish union issued a statement on Friday dismissing the idea. The IRFU noted that the opportunity for supporters to watch teams at home remains a central part of the competition’s appeal.

lead.why: The IRFU has issued a definitive statement closing down speculation regarding the relocation of Six Nations fixtures to the United States.

teams.body: The prospect of staging a Six Nations match in the United States remains unresolved as talks continue between World Rugby and participating unions. The Irish Rugby Football Union has already stated they have no current plans to move a home game to North America, and reports indicate that England are equally unlikely to participate due to concerns over domestic match-day revenue.

teams.heading: Japan Rugby League One resolves dispute regarding naturalised player registration rules
teams.body: Japan Rugby League One has officially backtracked on contentious eligibility rules that would have restricted the status of naturalised players. Following legal challenges and a significant backlash from players and fans, the league announced on 28 August that those who acquired Japanese citizenship, or applied for it, by May 2025 will now be treated as native-born players. Managing Executive Director Hajime Shoji admitted the league "lacked communication" with the affected parties, conceding they had "underestimated the reaction" to the initial proposal.

lead.why: The resolution of the league's player eligibility dispute is the most significant structural update for the domestic game.

teams.heading: John Plumtree questions if All Blacks need to select bigger players
teams.body: Following a 3-1 series defeat to the Springboks, assistant coach John Plumtree has admitted New Zealand may need to prioritise size to match South Africa’s physical intensity. Plumtree noted that the All Blacks appeared passive in the 22 during the final Test in Baltimore, struggling to contain direct runners. He stated, “If it’s a physical thing and these guys are just too big for us, then they have to start picking some bigger players,” acknowledging that forward supremacy remains a primary concern.

lead.why: John Plumtree’s assessment of the All Blacks' physical shortcomings has dominated the post-series analysis.

teams.heading: South Africa seal series win over New Zealand with Baltimore victory
teams.body: South Africa confirmed a 3-1 series triumph over New Zealand last Saturday, claiming a 43-28 win at M&T Bank Stadium in Baltimore. After conceding an early try, the Springboks leveraged their trademark forward dominance and bench depth to pull away, scoring six tries in the final Test. The match drew a crowd of 68,173, the largest ever to watch a rugby match in the United States, effectively closing out a physically demanding contest that has stress-tested the world champions.

lead.why: The series victory against New Zealand is the headline result currently dominating all rugby coverage.
